name: Neal Ferraro
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember keeping a child's drawing of a house I didn't own.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Neal by a small Thursday habit. Neal checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: My kid draws the bungalow every day. The tenant and daughter both asked for a copy and neither asked to be in it.
appearance: Neal has a loose dark braid, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Neal steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To give both women a copy of the child's drawing.
family: David Ramos is Neal’s older relative by marriage. Neal puts the kettle on. David chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The boy on the corner*, David says, “I live over the corner shop. I like the boy and I hate what brings people to our door.”
connections: Hollis Osei. A penciled drawing gives both women a chance to say what they recognize as home.

reactions.situation: An elderly gardener wants to move just one tree
reactions.response: Neal checks that the tree can survive the move before it is lifted.
